Stefan,

I attempted to find the calculation you mentioned at AAAL but was unable to. If you could point me in the right direction that would be awesome.  Just to ask the group as a whole, we (psst.byu.edu) are researching correlations between our oral proficiency test and the OPI (Oral Proficiency Interview) and I'm trying to estimate how many OPIs we need to collect. I am trying to figure out how many OPI scores we need (along with their test scores on our test) so that we don't over-fit our model. Any suggestions would be welcome.

Thanks,

messages.author: 5c92383d593d2a9a
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: Compensating for Over fitting variables
parts: On Mar 26, 2009, at 11:45 PM, Ross Hendrickson wrote:

> yes that is exactly it, although the end goal is to create the best
> model to do prediction with.

If you care about accuracy rather than model simplicity and
interpretability, I would at least try an SVM (for regression). R has
a simple to use SVM package called e1071 which will certainly be fast
enough for your situation. (You may or may not need more data; I'd
try though.)

To avoid overfitting while maximizing the use of training material,
you could do cross-validation, training on all data points except one
(the one that is used for evaluation). The same goes for a linear
regression model of course.

- David

--

messages.author: 5c92383d593d2a9a
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: Compensating for Over fitting variables
parts:
> Thanks for the reply, question though: I have looked into k-fold
> cross validation measures, mainly when I was using WEKA to explore
> other options / models but am curious as to how cross validating
> eliminates the possible over fitting of the data.

Have a look at Andrew Moore's slides:

www-personal.umich.edu/~danjl/teaching/slides/cross_validation.pdf

SVMs are "large-margin classifiers" that use structural risk
minimization to minimize overfitting. You'd still apply cross-
validation to them, particularly in order to estimate their parameters.
See also Tom Mitchell's slides:

www.cs.cmu.edu/~awm/15781/2003/Overfitting-MDL-StrucRisk.pdf

- David
